lessons.status: adopted scoped guidance; engine enforcement unqualified
lessons.detector_status: specified; not implemented or qualified by this corpus update
lessons.trigger: Before quoting a result, admitting a module, closing a parent or presenting done in a client.
lessons.antipattern: Self-certification, a summary of a summary, a skipped prerequisite, or a note/file count represented as runtime readiness.
lessons.good_pattern: Report a typed scoped verdict with exact candidate, admitted criteria, required checks, raw evidence, gaps and a counter-evidence pointer.
lessons.mechanism: The verifier receives the expected obligation set from its independent owner, not a subset supplied by the producer; accepted integrated code remains factual primary truth.
lessons.detector: Compare expected versus observed sets, exact subject/profile identities, exit/diagnostic evidence and all required dispositions; refuse empty, stale, invalid or missing coverage.
lessons.intended_fault: A producer omits a failing mandatory check and supplies a green summary; parent acceptance must refuse.
lessons.benign_mirror: The same complete subject with independently collected passing observations and no unresolved obligations is eligible for admission review.
lessons.placement: At result ingestion and immediately before claim/admission; UI rendering cannot promote the underlying state.
lessons.limits: Current v1 receipts and corpus publication prove scoped consistency only. No runtime admission collector exists. Independent review is useful but does not authenticate raw evidence by itself.
lessons.retirement: Revise after a demonstrated false pass or false refusal; never redefine pass to exclude the observed defect.

lessons.status: adopted scoped guidance; engine enforcement unqualified
lessons.detector_status: specified; not implemented or qualified by this corpus update
lessons.trigger: Before a new or changed detector is allowed to establish a clean result.
lessons.antipattern: A control that never reaches the real detector, measures the live world instead of its fixture, or is edited merely to turn the detector green.
lessons.good_pattern: Bind an intended-fault fixture and a benign mirror to the exact production check path, with a stable fault definition and expected diagnostic.
lessons.mechanism: Fixture identity, execution path and oracle are reviewed independently; prove sensitivity and specificity before relying on scans.
lessons.detector: Require actual intended-fault reachability and rejection for the right reason plus successful benign execution; record unmeasured or invalid fixture outcomes distinctly.
lessons.intended_fault: A supposed stale-receipt fixture accidentally reads the current live receipt; the harness must classify the experiment invalid.
lessons.benign_mirror: A bounded reader using a limit before allocation is accepted; do not ban the method name regardless of context.
lessons.placement: During detector qualification before the consequential gate, and after changing detector, fixture or admitted profile.
lessons.limits: Reading a reflection is not assimilation proof. These case designs are not implemented tests or primary case credits.
lessons.retirement: Repair the detector or harness when a counterexample survives; changes to the fault definition require a separate reviewed rationale.

lessons.title: Put the bound before allocation and the guard before effect

evidence.section: Related failures of the same family

6 · Wrote a bound and did not check that it bounded anything

lessons.status: adopted scoped guidance; engine enforcement unqualified
lessons.detector_status: specified; not implemented or qualified by this corpus update
lessons.trigger: Before parsing, allocation, fan-out, queue insertion, process launch or an irreversible effect.
lessons.antipattern: Truncating after an unbounded read, limiting after split, or running an authorization/quality check after the action.
lessons.good_pattern: Bound input acquisition and concurrency at the boundary; validate identities, capabilities and constraints before dispatch.
lessons.mechanism: A typed bounded input and admitted dispatch path make the unsafe order unavailable; include backpressure and explicit overflow/refusal.
lessons.detector: Observe peak acquisition/queue behavior and effect ordering under oversize input, saturation and denied admission.
lessons.intended_fault: An oversized stream must be refused before whole-input allocation and a denied service action must never reach its owner.
lessons.benign_mirror: An exact-limit stream and an authorized bounded request succeed through the same path.
lessons.placement: Inside the acquisition/dispatch boundary, not only in a later audit.
lessons.limits: Not a blanket ban on APIs that have safe bounded forms. Choose numerical and byte bounds from declared contracts, not inherited constants.
lessons.retirement: Revise bounds with measured workloads and resource budgets; retain refusal tests and do not trade correctness for a cosmetically clean scan.

lessons.title: One semantic owner across every consumer surface

lessons.status: adopted scoped guidance; engine enforcement unqualified
lessons.detector_status: specified; not implemented or qualified by this corpus update
lessons.trigger: When adding a CLI, tool, Pi, Bash, workflow or cross-language entry point.
lessons.antipattern: Two implementations of one rule drift; a callee reacquires an input from ambient state after being given the authoritative value.
lessons.good_pattern: Use one typed owner and thin projections; pass source, environment, task and caller identities explicitly and preserve the return contract.
lessons.mechanism: Reuse the existing 21-action catalogue and module dependency graph. Wrappers project arguments/results and cannot invent acceptance or grants.
lessons.detector: Differentially exercise equivalent CLI/UDS/tool requests and compare owner dispatch, permission, errors, cancellation and readback.
lessons.intended_fault: One wrapper accepts a forbidden effect or chooses an ambient target directory instead of the explicit one.
lessons.benign_mirror: Equivalent valid requests through all admitted surfaces produce equivalent semantic results with transport-specific presentation only.
lessons.placement: At interface contract review and consumer integration qualification before release.
lessons.limits: Does not require a new RPC, crate, daemon or globally public Rust symbol. Exact consumers and compatibility ranges govern visibility.
lessons.retirement: Retire redundant wrappers only after proving consumer replacement; version breaking changes and update both ends of the flow.

lessons.status: adopted scoped guidance; engine enforcement unqualified
lessons.detector_status: specified; not implemented or qualified by this corpus update
lessons.trigger: At re-entry, before evaluation or hardening, and before updating a completion claim.
lessons.antipattern: A familiar path, branch label, timestamp, commit message, cached binary or old receipt is treated as the measured subject.
lessons.good_pattern: Bind the actual source/artifact, dependencies, fixtures, toolchain and environment to the run; distinguish intended branch, current checkout and installed artifact.
lessons.mechanism: Content identity and explicit scope prevent proximity from masquerading as identity. Recheck changed subjects before carrying old success forward.
lessons.detector: Compare retained digests/revisions and current readback; inspect expected files and nonempty payloads before accepting results.
lessons.intended_fault: A receipt for an older subject, empty plan file or different installed binary must remain stale/invalid despite a success label.
lessons.benign_mirror: The unchanged exact subject with complete matching evidence remains applicable within its stated scope.
lessons.placement: Before expensive probes and again at claim/admission/publication.
lessons.limits: Mtime is a cheap clue, not proof of semantic freshness. This atlas is not a Git repository; do not invent a branch/commit. Historical receipts retain their original subject.
lessons.retirement: Supersede claims with the new observation and reason; never refresh only a timestamp or erase the original counterexample.

lessons.status: adopted scoped guidance; engine enforcement unqualified
lessons.detector_status: specified; not implemented or qualified by this corpus update
lessons.trigger: Before reproducibility, isolation or deployment claims and when crossing host, Toolbx and disposable worker boundaries.
lessons.antipattern: Warm caches, resident services or ambient mounts supply the answer; a read from one layer is reported as a fact about another.
lessons.good_pattern: Use explicit environment/toolchain/cache/workspace identities and independent output roots; qualify cold build, service state and installation separately.
lessons.mechanism: Remove undeclared shared state from the tested boundary and record what remains warm; source read-only custody is one control among several.
lessons.detector: Run the same meaningful candidate in declared clean and admitted warm profiles; check actual mount/process/environment identities and useful boundary results.
lessons.intended_fault: A nested build silently shares its parent target directory, or a tool from Toolbx inspects the wrong host path.
lessons.benign_mirror: Explicit isolated target/output directories and correctly routed host observations preserve the expected result.
lessons.placement: At environment construction and before assigning evidence to a deployment subject.
lessons.limits: No claim of a cold machine from a fresh build directory. Rootless execution still has security boundaries; SELinux z/Z are not universal ro fixes. Historical performance numbers are not current benchmarks.
lessons.retirement: Adjust profiles when the supported environment changes; retain exact identities and disclose unavailable environments rather than counting them as pass.

lessons.title: Preserve producer verdict and process custody

evidence.section: The set that transfers regardless of substrate
35 - An agent working under my brief killed another session's mutation run, and my brief had not said the one rule that would have stopped it
38 - I started a job that was already running, then read its progress from a count that also prints on failure

lessons.status: adopted scoped guidance; engine enforcement unqualified
lessons.detector_status: specified; not implemented or qualified by this corpus update
lessons.trigger: Before shell chaining, retrying a job, cancelling a process or presenting progress as success.
lessons.antipattern: A pipeline consumer hides producer failure; a pattern kill or duplicate launch affects another agent; progress counters appear on both failure and success.
lessons.good_pattern: Capture the decisive producer status and raw output, keep explicit job/process/session identities and check existing obligations before retry or cleanup.
lessons.mechanism: Thin argv-safe wrappers preserve status. One lifecycle owner controls each job; cancellation acknowledgement and verified settlement are separate.
lessons.detector: Exercise failing producer through display/log pipelines, broken pipes, lost acknowledgements, duplicate starts and reused process identities.
lessons.intended_fault: A failing producer followed by a successful formatter must still fail; an unrelated matching process must remain untouched.
lessons.benign_mirror: A successful producer retains success through the same wrapper; cancellation addresses only the owned current job and verifies settlement.
lessons.placement: Before command execution, retry and cleanup; not just a session-end detector.
lessons.limits: PID alone does not establish identity. Do not copy diary pkill commands or prescribe blanket termination. No process cleanup or service changes are performed here.
lessons.retirement: If the same trap recurs, test actual invocation coverage and move enforcement to the real entry path; do not add another prose warning only.

lessons.status: adopted scoped guidance; engine enforcement unqualified
lessons.detector_status: specified; not implemented or qualified by this corpus update
lessons.trigger: When designing module tests, fixing lint diagnostics or reporting a hardening result.
lessons.antipattern: Padding the 50-case floor, weakening the oracle, broad lint suppression, deferred mutation evidence or a handwritten zero-warning label.
lessons.good_pattern: Retain at least 50 distinct meaningful module-owned cases and zero baseline warnings/errors on every admitted profile; repair code and close material gaps.
lessons.mechanism: Use the existing testing standard and case ownership rules; independent oracles, assimilation pairs and a nonempty mutation campaign remain separate obligations.
lessons.detector: Inspect executed case identities, profile coverage, raw diagnostics and mutation survivors; reject skip/zero/stale results and unapproved rule changes.
lessons.intended_fault: Fifty names that execute no behavior, one skipped required profile or a surviving material mutant must not qualify.
lessons.benign_mirror: A meaningful complete suite with zero baseline diagnostics and reviewed mutation/assimilation evidence is eligible for qualification.
lessons.placement: At test design, after repairs and before module/integrated acceptance; applicable doctests and package checks are included.
lessons.limits: The diary discussion of a possible test-count override does not authorize one here. Its historical single-assertion criticism was corrected; assertion count is not a quality metric. No new blanket suppression permission is adopted.
lessons.retirement: Improve coverage after counterexamples; do not lower the user floor or redefine the diagnostic budget to match existing output.

lessons.trigger: When recalling a lesson, updating a roster observation or projecting a changed accepted module.
lessons.antipattern: An old confident statement is read as current; a new date replaces evidence; generated copies become competing truth.
lessons.good_pattern: Retain original source/hash/date/scope, adoption decision and supersession reason; accepted code owns current implemented facts and requirements retain their owner.
lessons.mechanism: Use the existing catalogue/receipt projections and stable module/source anchors. A diary reflection can motivate a rule but cannot grant runtime authority.
lessons.detector: Compare live source content and captured subject, identify obsolete assertions and surface current-versus-desired differences with a review queue.
lessons.intended_fault: A source changes under an adopted lesson while the old snapshot is still described as live/current.

lessons.placement: At intake, context assembly, publication and re-entry before acting on recalled claims.

lessons.retirement: Mark superseded/rejected lessons with the deciding evidence and successor; preserve originals and update all consumer routes.

lessons.status: adopted scoped guidance; engine enforcement unqualified

lessons.trigger: When selecting a prototype component, optional neural operator, new helper or inherited working pattern.
lessons.antipattern: Prototype gravity, imported jargon/persona, or an inherited architecture is mistaken for a validated v3 design.
lessons.good_pattern: Name the local problem, smallest useful mechanism, evidence gained, commitment justified and what can be discarded.
lessons.mechanism: Reuse existing module owners and optional task gates; copy neither old deployment state nor unqualified identities/credentials into the new engine.
lessons.detector: Compare the proposed addition against existing owners and actual consumer need; require bounded success/failure criteria and an explicit reject/defer disposition.
lessons.intended_fault: An optional operator or prototype service becomes a mandatory dependency without an admitted measured benefit.
lessons.benign_mirror: A scoped component idea improves a declared task under held-out evaluation, or is rejected without harming baseline operation.
lessons.placement: At architecture changes and prototype exit before adoption or deployment.
lessons.limits: Historic prototype counts and top-tail ambitions are not v3 performance evidence. No personality or awareness claims are adopted from the diary.
lessons.retirement: Retire scaffolding or an experiment when its question is answered; keep the lesson and evidence rather than preserving machinery by inertia.

lessons.status: adopted scoped guidance; engine enforcement unqualified
lessons.detector_status: specified; not implemented or qualified by this corpus update
lessons.trigger: At delegation, handoff, shared-resource access and every meaningful task/phase boundary.
lessons.antipattern: Duplicate construction packets, unowned mutation runs, overlapping writes or a brief that omits the rule protecting another thread.
lessons.good_pattern: Give each thread one bounded objective, subject/brief revision, resource/write ownership, dependencies, limits, return schema and cleanup obligations.
lessons.mechanism: The existing cohort/task owner coordinates claims and joins; context carries relevant lessons and dissent. Child success cannot accept the parent.
lessons.detector: Check ownership overlap, duplicate active jobs, stale brief revisions, omitted required children and integrated evidence at the parent join.
lessons.intended_fault: Two agents mutate the same workspace or one kills an unowned job; a child passes against a superseded brief.
lessons.benign_mirror: Disjoint owned work returns compatible candidates, evidence and gaps; the parent integrates and verifies the actual combined subject.
lessons.placement: Before dispatch and before joins; reassert relevant standards at phase boundaries without inventing an arbitrary runtime ritual.
lessons.limits: Different model families can add perspective but do not guarantee correctness or independent collector custody. Do not add a second scheduler.
lessons.retirement: Change coordination when observed conflict/duplication justifies it; measure overhead and avoid copying every lesson into every brief.

lessons.trigger: Before trusting a metric, known-answer fixture, statistical comparison or a confident correction.
lessons.antipattern: The metric samples the wrong domain, a test oracle is wrong, or humility/praise substitutes for observation.
lessons.good_pattern: Define the measured construct, population, denominator and exclusions; independently check the oracle and record falsifiers, uncertainty and changed conclusions.

lessons.detector: Use representative boundary cases and counterexamples; compare independent oracle/results and inspect all admitted domain coverage.
lessons.intended_fault: A numeric residual is negative despite an actual survivor, or a thematic regex measures writing style instead of the claimed construct.

lessons.placement: Before evaluation results guide routing, cohort policy or completion reports; recheck after changing the instrument.
lessons.limits: The diary thematic percentages and correlation claims remain historical and were not reproduced. No inherited 10x/top-7% effect is asserted.
lessons.retirement: Invalidate conclusions when the construct or instrument fails; rerun the question rather than merely editing the sentence that reported it.

lessons.trigger: Before calling an integration connected, a deployment useful or a restore complete.

lessons.good_pattern: Send a real bounded request through the supported seam and verify useful return/readback; declare durable state and independently test restoration.

lessons.status: adopted scoped guidance; engine enforcement unqualified

lessons.trigger: When adding another rule, helper, generated note, verification stage or repeated context packet.
lessons.antipattern: Unmeasured scripts and notes grow while only Rust is budgeted; repeated prose changes never reach an action; a newly authored helper is never used.
lessons.good_pattern: Prefer one existing owner and reusable entry point. Record the problem, placement, footprint, verification cost, prevented failure, false-positive/rework cost and retirement condition.

lessons.benign_mirror: A justified module-linked lesson is reachable, its maintained projection runs through the existing command and its scope/cost are explicit.
lessons.placement: At assimilation proposal, corpus publication and workflow review; do not infer usefulness from elapsed effort or file counts.
lessons.limits: This update measures documentation/maintenance footprint only. Prevention rate and engine workflow benefit remain unmeasured; counts are not a performance score.

conflicts_and_limits.claim: A 50-test floor might permit a documented override.
conflicts_and_limits.disposition: Not adopted as permission. The active v3 requirement remains at least 50 meaningful module-owned cases; no filler and no silent override.

conflicts_and_limits.claim: Historic start-coding gates, mining and cockpit re-entry commands.
conflicts_and_limits.disposition: Historical HEE-v2 instructions are not v3 authorization. No mining, respawn, service activation or runtime implementation is performed from note commands.

conflicts_and_limits.claim: Use :z rather than :Z as a universal fix for read-only mounts.
conflicts_and_limits.disposition: Not adopted. Podman documents ro/rw separately from z/Z; z requests shared SELinux labeling and Z private labeling. Relabeling depends on host permissions and context. No automatic relabel or SELinux disable is prescribed.

conflicts_and_limits.claim: Rootless containers remove security boundaries and read-only sources make contamination impossible.
conflicts_and_limits.disposition: Not adopted literally. Rootless mode and read-only mounts are scoped controls; shared outputs, credentials, network, user namespaces and host/container custody still require qualification.

conflicts_and_limits.claim: Historic thematic percentages, correlations and a proposed future rerun.
conflicts_and_limits.disposition: Retained as historical interpretation. The reflection reports missing replay tooling; this update does not reproduce those metrics or infer causal improvement.

conflicts_and_limits.claim: Inherited traits or identity imply reliable behavior.
conflicts_and_limits.disposition: No persona/identity is imported. Transfer only specific observed failure classes, triggers and falsifiable verification obligations.

conflicts_and_limits.claim: Blanket method bans, arbitrary antipattern numbering or mandatory self-criticism.
conflicts_and_limits.disposition: Use the local LRN namespace, consumer-specific invariants and measured evidence. Do not ban safe bounded forms or manufacture weaknesses.
